latest_observation.visible_state: Chrome extension observation reached the completed ChatGPT Deep Research report. Visible metadata showed Research completed in 9m, 6 citations, 120 searches, report title Benchmark Raw Output, run metadata Status: completed, and the correct light_structured run ID. The report body is visible in a cross-origin Deep Research iframe, but extension-safe probes exposed only the shell: full Chrome browser-client tab control, top-level DOM, iframe locators, direct sandbox tabs, page storage, response menus, View sources, View files in chat, conversation options, Share modals, Chrome content.export/exportGsuite, browser.tabs.content, dev logs, backend conversation fetch, page-eval fetch/XHR/script-injection, Copy response, and virtual clipboard paths did not expose raw Markdown. The full Chrome runtime can reach the target tab and exposes Playwright, DOM CUA, dev-log, clipboard, and tab content APIs. The response More actions menu exposed timestamp, View sources, and Branch in new chat; the View sources panel reported No additional sources found and no export, download, or Markdown control. The current conversation options menu exposed Share, Start a group chat, View files in chat, Move to project, Pin chat, Archive, and Delete, but no export, download, Markdown, or raw report control. View files in chat reported No files referenced yet. Page storage had no localStorage/sessionStorage matches and no IndexedDB or Cache Storage surface in the extension evaluation context. The top and response Share modals exposed Copy link and LinkedIn controls, but no report body, native Markdown, export, download, or raw report control; Copy link was not used. browser.tabs.content rejected text, HTML, and DOM snapshot extraction as unsupported by the Chrome backend, and its schema rejects markdown/md/visibleText/accessibilityTree content types before command dispatch. No Browser plugin, Computer Use, coordinate clicking, AppleScript/JXA, generic desktop automation, OCR, screenshot reconstruction, or desktop-control fallback was used.

harvest_probe_attempts.method: full Chrome browser-client runtime tab inspection
harvest_probe_attempts.notes: The Chrome plugin runtime connected to the extension backend, listed the existing ChatGPT tabs, and retrieved the target tab with Playwright, DOM CUA, dev-log, clipboard, and tab content APIs available; those APIs still exposed only the ChatGPT shell, prompt metadata, empty Deep Research iframe body, and response controls, not raw report Markdown.

The extension schema allows only html, text, and domSnapshot content types; markdown, md, visibleText, and accessibilityTree are rejected by schema, and the Chrome backend rejects tabs_content for html, text, and domSnapshot.
Top-level visible DOM exposed ChatGPT shell, user prompt, and response controls, but not the Deep Research report metadata or body.
Top-level page exposed a cross-origin Deep Research iframe, but frame textContent and body innerText were empty through extension-safe locator access.
Direct sandbox tabs were visible to the Chrome extension but contained only a blank sandbox skeleton with no report body, buttons, or links.
The response menu exposed timestamp, View sources, and Branch in new chat, but no download, export, copy Markdown, or raw report control.

harvest_probe_attempts.method: View sources panel inspection from response More actions menu

The current conversation menu exposed Share, Start a group chat, View files in chat, Move to project, Pin chat, Archive, and Delete; it exposed no export, download, Markdown, copy, or raw report control.
